aria-current="page"><span class="text-truncate">Virtual Shadow Maps</span><!----><!----></li><!----><!----><!----><!----></ol><!----></nav></div><!----></div><!----><h1>Virtual Shadow Maps</h1><p class="text-secondary mb-0"> Learn about the high-resolution shadow techniques designed with film-quality assets and large dynamically lit open worlds in mind. </p><!----></header><!----><div class="row"><div class="col-lg-9 print-w-100"><div class="b-img"><img class="img-fluid" alt="Virtual Shadow Maps" width="1920" height="335" loading="lazy" fetchpriority="auto" decoding="auto" ng-img="true" src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/dd434226-d488-4940-b82b-276c044acf4e?resizing_type=fill&width=1920&height=335" https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/dd434226-d488-4940-b82b-276c044acf4e?resizing_type=fill&width=3840&height=670 2x"></div><!----><!----><!----><header class="document-header 42rem;"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><strong>Virtual Shadow Maps</strong> (VSMs) is the new shadow mapping method used to deliver consistent, high-resolution shadowing that works with film-quality assets and large, dynamically lit open worlds using Unreal Engine 5's <a data-document-id="4596095" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/nanite-in-unreal-engine">Nanite Virtualized Geometry</a>, <a data-document-id="3224923" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/lumen-global-illumination-and-reflections-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.5">Lumen Global Illumination and Reflections</a>, and <a data-document-id="3225331" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/world-partition-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.5">World Partition</a> features.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="goals-of-virtual-shadow-maps" data-previous-ids="goalsofvirtualshadowmaps"> Goals of Virtual Shadow Maps </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Virtual Shadow Maps have been developed with the following goals:</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Significantly increase shadow resolution to match highly detailed Nanite geometry</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Plausible soft shadows with reasonable, controllable performance costs</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Provide a simple solution that works by default with limited amounts of adjustment needed</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Replace the many Stationary Light shadowing techniques with a single, unified path</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Conceptually, virtual shadow maps are just very high-resolution shadow maps. In their current implementation, they have a virtual resolution of 16k x 16k pixels. Clipmaps are used to increase resolution further for Directional Lights. To keep performance high at reasonable memory cost, VSMs split the shadow map into tiles (or Pages) that are 128x128 each. Pages are allocated and rendered only as needed to shade on-screen pixels based on an analysis of the depth buffer. The pages are cached between frames unless they are invalidated by moving objects or light, which further improves performance.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-note"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-info-circle text-body-secondary"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Nanite does not support many of the Stationary Light shadowing techniques, such as pre-shadows and per-object (or Inset) shadows. While some of the more dynamic parts of Stationary Light shadowing may work — such as the Cascaded Shadow Maps near the camera viewer — Nanite and Stationary Lights with conventional shadow maps are not supported. If you are using Nanite in your project, you must either use Movable Lights or use Virtual Shadow Maps.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="enabling-virtual-shadow-maps" data-previous-ids="enablingvirtualshadowmaps"> Enabling Virtual Shadow Maps </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">In the Project Settings under <strong>Engine > Rendering</strong> in the <strong>Shadows</strong> section, you can set what <strong>Shadow Map Method</strong> your project supports, whether <strong>Virtual Shadow Maps</strong> or the conventional <strong>Shadow Maps</strong> that have been used in previous Unreal Engine releases.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-note"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-info-circle text-body-secondary"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Projects created with versions before Unreal Engine 5.0 will need to opt-in using the project setting, or console variable <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.Enable</code>. New projects use Virtual Shadow Maps by default.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-warning"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-exclamation-circle-filled text-warning"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Virtual Shadow Maps are designed to be used with <b>Nanite</b>. If your target platform or project does not use Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps is likely not a good fit.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-image class="block-image"><div class="block-image"><figure class="figure"><a href="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/7ef5dffd-a3e1-4b6e-9672-8046db99b8a2?resizing_type=fit"><picture><!----><source media="(min-width: 768px)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/7ef5dffd-a3e1-4b6e-9672-8046db99b8a2?resizing_type=fit&width=1400&height=656"><!----><source media="(min-width: 0)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/7ef5dffd-a3e1-4b6e-9672-8046db99b8a2?resizing_type=fit&width=768&height=360"><!----><img class="figure-img img-fluid" src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/7ef5dffd-a3e1-4b6e-9672-8046db99b8a2?resizing_type=fit" alt="" width="1200" height="562" data-caption=""></picture></a><!----><!----><!----></figure></div><!----></block-image><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h3 id="what-happens-with-existing-shadow-methods-when-vs-ms-are-enabled" data-previous-ids="whathappenswithexistingshadowmethodswhenvsmsareenabled?"> What happens with existing shadow methods when VSMs are enabled? </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">When VSMs are enabled, they replace a variety of existing shadow methods in Unreal Engine:</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Stationary precomputed shadows, including 2D Distance Field and shadow factor "shadow maps"</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Pre-shadows</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Per-object / inset shadows</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSMs)</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Movable dynamic shadows for local lights</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Fully baked shadows from Static Lights will still work as before (when not using Lumen). Their contributions are entirely represented in the baked lightmaps and there is no runtime lighting evaluated at all. Stationary lights will use the indirect diffuse contribution from any baked lightmaps, but their direct lighting and shadows are evaluated dynamically (the same as Movable lights) when VSMs are enabled.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><a data-document-id="3225039" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/distance-field-soft-shadows-in-unreal-engine">Distance Field Shadows</a> are not replaced, and can be used in tandem with Virtual Shadow Maps for Directional Lights. Distance Field Shadows take over for non-Nanite geometry beyond the dynamic shadowing distance of Movable Lights — set on a Directional Light using the Cascaded Shadow Maps property <strong>Dynamic Shadow Distance Movable Light</strong>. Using Distance Field Shadows provides a useful tool to reduce runtime costs in complex scenes, such as those with lots of <a data-document-id="3225183" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/virtual-shadow-maps-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.5">non-Nanite foliage</a>.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Nanite geometry always renders to the Virtual Shadow Map regardless of distance, since this is the most performant option and provides the highest quality. It is possible to make non-Nanite geometry behave the same way as Nanite by the console variable <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.UseFarShadowCulling 0</code>.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Local lights (Point and Spot Lights) are not affected, and selecting Distance Field shadows for these continues to override the active shadow map method.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Due to VSM's high resolution and accuracy, the screen space Contact Shadow feature controlled with the Contact Shadow Length property is no longer necessary to achieve sharp contact shadows. It still may have value when used to pick up cheaper shadows from objects set to not render into shadow maps but is not recommended otherwise as it will be less accurate than the shadows VSMs will create.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Ray-traced shadows still take precedence over VSMs as they generally provide the highest quality solution.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="soft-shadows-with-shadow-map-ray-tracing" data-previous-ids="softshadowswithshadowmapraytracing"> Soft Shadows with Shadow Map Ray Tracing </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><strong>Shadow Map Ray Tracing</strong> (SMRT) is a sampling algorithm used with virtual shadow maps to produce more plausible soft shadows and contact hardening. Objects that cast shadows farther will have softer shadows than objects casting shadows closer to a shadow-receiving surface.
For example, the mesh pictured below is tall and casts its shadow over a long distance. Shadows near the base are sharper than those farther away.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-image class="block-image"><div internallinkhandler="">The SMRT algorithm works by shooting a number of rays towards the light source, but instead of evaluating intersections with geometry — like conventional raytracing does — a number of samples along the ray are projected and tested against the virtual shadow map to achieve soft shadowing and contact hardening.
Shadow rays are distributed based on the light using <strong>Source Radius</strong> on local lights or <strong>Source Angle</strong> on Directional Lights.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><div internallinkhandler="">Local lights have no Source Radius by default, compared to Directional Lights which start with a low Source Angle. When either are set with an appropriate value, SMRT produces real-time soft shadowing with contact hardening, like the example below using a Point Light with a Source Radius of 10.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><div block-comparison-slider="" class="block-comparison-slider" _nghost-serverapp-c221070999=""><div class="img-before"><img src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/4f52a022-7213-4eb9-ae37-8f28fd6b4ff6?resizing_type=fit&width=1920&height=1080" alt="Point Light with Source Radius 0"></div><div class="img-after"><img src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/bbf9d6e6-8998-43d8-8433-4623184ecdc7?resizing_type=fit&width=1920&height=1080" alt="Point Light with Source Radius 10"></div><input _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" class="slider"><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="slider-thumb"><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="slider-thumb-img"></div></div><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="caption-before">Point Light with Source Radius 0</div><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="caption-after">Point Light with Source Radius 10</div></div><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h3 id="controlling-penumbra-shadow-quality" data-previous-ids="controllingpenumbrashadowquality"> Controlling Penumbra Shadow Quality </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">The penumbra shadow's softness and quality is set by console variables for both local and Directional Lights. They include their own scalability settings that are generally good for most scenes.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-tip"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-lightbulb tip-icon-color"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Noise in the penumbra is influenced by the number of rays being used, and both local and Directional Lights use eight rays by default when scalability for <strong>Shadows</strong> is set to <strong>Epic</strong>.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Use the console variables <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.RayCountLocal</code> and <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.RayCountDirectional</code> to adjust the number of rays. Fewer rays show visible noise in the penumbra. Setting the associated console variable to 0 disables SMRT and reverts to single-sample hard shadows.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><div block-comparison-slider="" class="block-comparison-slider" _nghost-serverapp-c221070999=""><div class="img-before"><img src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/a9544395-836a-462b-ad57-4932321b3fcc?resizing_type=fit&width=1920&height=1080" alt="Directional Light Source Angle: 5.0 | SMRT Ray Count: 1"></div><div class="img-after"><img src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/d72cac61-5540-49ce-a23f-ef6477f2f31a?resizing_type=fit&width=1920&height=1080" alt="Directional Light Source Angle: 5.0 | SMRT Ray Count: 7 (Default)"></div><input _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" class="slider"><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="slider-thumb"><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="slider-thumb-img"></div></div><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="caption-before">Directional Light Source Angle: 5.0 | SMRT Ray Count: 1</div><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="caption-after">Directional Light Source Angle: 5.0 | SMRT Ray Count: 7 (Default)</div></div><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Furthermore, the number of shadow samples taken along each ray's path can be set for both local and Directional Lights to control the maximum softness. Fewer shadow map samples are cheaper to render, but limit the amount of penumbra softness that can be achieved by the light's shadows.
For finer control than the <strong>Shadow</strong> scalability settings, and the console variables <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.SamplesPerRayLocal</code> and <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.SamplesPerRayDirectional</code> to adjust the number of samples used. Using values between 4 and 8 samples works well.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-slider-sequence id="limitations-of-shadow-map-ray-tracing" data-previous-ids="limitationsofshadowmapraytracing"> Limitations of Shadow Map Ray Tracing </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Quality of SMRT is generally good with the default setting, but there are limitations inherent to using the data from a single shadow map projection rather than testing against true geometry.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h3 id="penumbra-size-limits" data-previous-ids="penumbrasizelimits"> Penumbra Size Limits </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">The shadow's penumbra is clamped for local and Directional Lights to avoid sample divergence from the ray origin that can become increasingly "bent" compared to the ideal test along the ray itself. Using reasonable values for Source Radius on local lights and Source Angle on Directional Lights will avoid results that are too extreme, limiting the extent that the ray can diverge in various ways. Values that are too large can both impact performance and cause shadow penumbrae to visually warp as the camera gets near to them.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-video class="block-video"><electra-player class="d-block ratio ratio-16x9"><iframe src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/cms/videos/V_8agTmX/embed.html"></iframe></electra-player><!----><!----></block-video><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Local and Directional Lights can use the console variables <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.MaxRayAngleFromLight</code> and <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.SMRT.RayLengthScaleDirectional</code> to loosen or tighten the clamped extents.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h3 id="inconsistent-penumbra" data-previous-ids="inconsistentpenumbra"> Inconsistent Penumbra </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Since the Virtual Shadow Map only stores the first depth layer where naive iteration misses intersections with any occluders behind the first one, a variety of light leaking artifacts can happen where the occluders overlap. These types of light leaks are resolved using a gap-filling heuristic that extrapolates depths behind the first occluder based on depths seen before the point of occlusion.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-image class="block-image"><div class="block-image"><figure class="figure"><a href="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/9da24067-dd36-4321-8a3a-aafd672700dd?resizing_type=fit"><picture><!----><source media="(min-width: 768px)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/9da24067-dd36-4321-8a3a-aafd672700dd?resizing_type=fit&width=1400&height=981"><!----><source media="(min-width: 0)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/9da24067-dd36-4321-8a3a-aafd672700dd?resizing_type=fit&width=768&height=538"><!----><img class="figure-img img-fluid" src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/9da24067-dd36-4321-8a3a-aafd672700dd?resizing_type=fit" alt="" width="1200" height="841" data-caption="Examples of inconsistent penumbra shadows."></picture></a><!----><!----><figcaption class="figure-caption"> Examples of inconsistent penumbra shadows. </figcaption><!----></figure></div><!----></block-image><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="clipmaps-for-directional-light" data-previous-ids="clipmapsfordirectionallight"> Clipmaps for Directional Light </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">A single virtual shadow map does not provide enough resolution to cover large areas. Directional Lights use a clipmap structure of expanding ranges around the camera, with each clipmap level having its own 16K VSM. Each clipmap level is the same resolution but covers twice the radius of the previous one.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><div internallinkhandler="">Directional Light Clipmap Visualization</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></td><td><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Virtual Shadow Map Pages Visualization</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></td><!----></tr><!----></tbody><!----><!----></table></div><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">By default, clipmap levels 6 through 22 are allocated virtual shadow map page tables. This means that the default settings have the most detailed clipmap covering 64 cm (2^6 cm) from the camera position, and the broadest clipmap covering about 40 kilometers (2^22 cm). The cost of virtual clipmap levels is insignificant if nothing is present in them, so these defaults work well to cover very large scenes with fairly high resolution near the camera.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-note"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-info-circle text-body-secondary"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">The first and last levels can be adjusted using the console variables r.Shadow.Virtual.Clipmap.FirstLevel and <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.Clipmap.LastLevel</code>.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">The resolution allocated to a given pixel is a function of the distance away from the clipmap origin — the camera. This is set by Shadow scalability with the console variable <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.ResolutionLodBiasDirectional</code>. A value of 0 picks the resolution required based on the perspective projection of the camera.
Projective aliasing — when a shadow is cast on a surface almost parallel to the light direction — is still possible, even at high resolutions, but it can be reduced partly by biasing the resolution. Like Mip biasing in textures, lowering the value by -1 doubles the resolution of shadows with the associated performance tradeoffs. </p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="local-lights" data-previous-ids="locallights"> Local Lights </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Spot Lights use a single 16k VSM with a mip chain rather than clipmaps to handle shadow level of detail. Similarly, Point Lights use a cube map of 16k VSMs, one for each face.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Local lights provide a significant increase in resolution compared to traditional shadow maps. It is possible to run out of virtual resolution with very large local lights, and care should be taken to use Directional Lights where possible in these cases.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><div block-comparison-slider="" class="block-comparison-slider" _nghost-serverapp-c221070999=""><div class="img-before"><img src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/91f53207-7faa-4359-86ee-b9f49aa96b63?resizing_type=fit&width=1920&height=1080" alt="Scene lit by a Spot Light"></div><div class="img-after"><img src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/6d0f8890-9a3e-44ac-86d4-ca5cea514f69?resizing_type=fit&width=1920&height=1080" alt="Virtual Shadow Map Pages for a Spot Light"></div><input _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50" class="slider"><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="slider-thumb"><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="slider-thumb-img"></div></div><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="caption-before">Scene lit by a Spot Light</div><div _ngcontent-serverapp-c221070999="" class="caption-after">Virtual Shadow Map Pages for a Spot Light</div></div><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Appropriate mip levels are picked by projecting the size of the screen pixels into shadow map space. Like Directional Lights, it's possible to bias the resolution with the Shadow scalability settings, or using the console variable <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.ResolutionLodBiasLocal</code>.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-note"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-info-circle text-body-secondary"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Per-light resolution controls are not available but may be added in a future release.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="caching"> Caching </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Reusing shadow map pages from previous frames is key to maintaining high performance with Virtual Shadow Maps, especially in complex scenes. Caching is enabled by default, but can disabled for debugging purposes using the console variable <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.Cache 0</code>. </p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Since pages are only rendered for on-screen pixels, changing camera visibility due to movement of disocclusion can reveal new pages that need to be rendered. Generally, as long as camera movement is relatively smooth, it is not a major source of new pages. On the other hand, you should watch out for very fast movement near objects, large disocclusions, and camera cuts.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">In most scenes, the largest source of work comes from shadow map pages that need to be redrawn due to changes in scene geometry. Common sources of cache page invalidations include:</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Any light movement or rotation will invalidate all cached pages for that light</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Geometry that casts shadows moving, or being added or removed from the scene will invalidate any pages that overlap its bounding box from the light's perspective.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">This can include objects such as Blueprints setting properties on primitive components that trigger render state invalidation even though it does not actually move.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Geometry using materials that may modify mesh positions, such as World Position Offset (WPO) or Pixel Depth Offset (PDO).</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h3 id="managing-cache-invalidations" data-previous-ids="managingcacheinvalidations"> Managing Cache Invalidations </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Decreasing cache invalidations is best done by first visualizing the invalidations, then finding and reducing the things causing them. The <a data-anchor-id="12005" data-document-id="3225183" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/virtual-shadow-maps-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.5#visualization">Cached Page visualization</a> is a good place to start.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-image class="block-image"><div class="block-image"><figure class="figure"><a href="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/982301c6-87b4-4bf9-97fc-0c371a5a7262?resizing_type=fit"><picture><source media="(min-width: 1400px)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/982301c6-87b4-4bf9-97fc-0c371a5a7262?resizing_type=fit&width=2800&height=1742"><!----><source media="(min-width: 768px)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/982301c6-87b4-4bf9-97fc-0c371a5a7262?resizing_type=fit&width=1400&height=871"><!----><source media="(min-width: 0)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/982301c6-87b4-4bf9-97fc-0c371a5a7262?resizing_type=fit&width=768&height=478"><!----><img class="figure-img img-fluid" src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/982301c6-87b4-4bf9-97fc-0c371a5a7262?resizing_type=fit" alt="Virtual Shadow Map Cached Page Visualization" width="2025" height="1260" data-caption="Cached Page Visualization"></picture></a><!----><!----><figcaption class="figure-caption"> Cached Page Visualization </figcaption><!----></figure></div><!----></block-image><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">In this visualization, pages that are fully cached are shaded <strong>green</strong>. Pages that are new or invalidated are shaded <strong>red</strong>. As you move the camera you should expect to see small rings of red near screen edges, clipmap boundaries and disoccluded geometry. With a static camera, most of the new pages will come from cache invalidations.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Once problem areas have been found, it is often additionally useful to inspect the objects and object bounds that are driving the invalidations using the <b>ShadowCasters</b> viewmode. Inspect these objects and bounds to ensure that they are indeed objects that are expected to invalidate shadows, and that their bounds are as tight as possible. Since all pages that an invalidating object could potentially overlap within its bounds must be invalidated, even moderately inflated bounds combined with low light angles can cause many unnecessary invalidations.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-image class="block-image"><div class="block-image"><figure class="figure"><a href="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b6324a5c-a405-47c7-9232-8b1d4f4f7663?resizing_type=fit"><picture><source media="(min-width: 1400px)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b6324a5c-a405-47c7-9232-8b1d4f4f7663?resizing_type=fit&width=2800&height=1738"><!----><source media="(min-width: 768px)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b6324a5c-a405-47c7-9232-8b1d4f4f7663?resizing_type=fit&width=1400&height=869"><!----><source media="(min-width: 0)" srcset="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b6324a5c-a405-47c7-9232-8b1d4f4f7663?resizing_type=fit&width=768&height=477"><!----><img class="figure-img img-fluid" src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/documentation/image/b6324a5c-a405-47c7-9232-8b1d4f4f7663?resizing_type=fit" alt="Virtual Shadow Maps ShadowCasters Visualization" width="2023" height="1256" data-caption="Virtual Shadow Maps ShadowCasters Visualization"></picture></a><!----><!----><figcaption class="figure-caption"> Virtual Shadow Maps ShadowCasters Visualization </figcaption><!----></figure></div><!----></block-image><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Invalidations that are entirely in the shadow of Nanite objects can be skipped, but this is not true for non-Nanite objects. For this reason it is particularly important to ensure that large shadow-casting objects — such as buildings — use <a data-document-id="4596246" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/nanite-virtualized-geometry-in-unreal-engine">Nanite</a>.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-tip"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-lightbulb tip-icon-color"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">You can trigger Virtual Shadow Map invalidation on Nanite LOD streaming changes with the console variable <code>r.Nanite.VSMInvalidateOnLODDelta</code>. Clusters that are not streamed into LOD matching the computed Nanite LOD estimate trigger VSM invalidation such that they are re-rendered when streaming completes. This functionality is experimental. We do not recommend shipping projects with Experimental features and this feature is subject to change.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">You can override default engine behavior for shadow invalidations with the per-primitive enumeration class Shadow Cache Invalidation Behavior. This is useful to prevent invalidations from static World Position Offset (WPO). The options include:</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><strong>Auto</strong>: (Default) Invalidates based on World Position Offset material and transform changes.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><strong>Always</strong>: Always invalidate shadows, can be used to flag a primitive that is using some method of animating that is not known to the system.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><strong>Rigid</strong>: Suppress invalidations that would otherwise be generated by, for example, World Position Offset.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><strong>Static</strong>: In addition to the <strong>Rigid</strong> behavior, also suppress invalidations due to transform changes. Add/Remove still triggers invalidations. If the primitive is moved or animated, the visual result is undefined.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h3 id="non-nanite-deformation-and-foliage" data-previous-ids="non-nanitedeformationandfoliage"> Deformation and Foliage </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Geometry that can be deformed using Skeletal animation, or materials using World Position Offset or Pixel Depth Offset always invalidates cached pages every frame. It is extremely important to ensure that these features are used carefully and bounds are kept under control.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">In some cases, such as grass and sometimes foliage, using only <a data-document-id="3225187" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/contact-shadows-in-unreal-engine">Contact Shadows</a> is a sufficient substitute for high resolution shadow maps. In cases where high detail shadows are necessary in the foreground, consider the following to help mitigate the performance cost:</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Non-Nanite objects still respect the regular shadow CPU culling settings, such as <code>r.Shadow.RadiusThreshold</code>. Use these to help control the cost of rendering these objects into Virtual Shadow Maps.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Use Mesh LODs to switch to materials that do not use WPO/PDO at distances where the effect is no longer obvious. In some cases, it may be possible to switch off dynamic shadow casting for these objects in the distance and rely entirely on screen space Contact Shadows.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">For Directional Lights, there are additional options available:</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Distance Field Shadows take over for non-Nanite geometry beyond the <strong>Dynamic Shadow Distance Movable Light</strong> distance set by the Cascaded Shadow Maps section of the Light. Switching to Distance Field Shadows for non-Nanite in the distance can be a large performance improvement since this geometry does not have the fine-grained LOD scaling that Nanite provides.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h4 id="disablingmeshdeformationatadistance"> Disabling Mesh Deformation at a Distance </h4><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Techniques such as World Position Offset (WPO), Pixel Depth Offset (PDO), tessellation, and skeletal animation are commonly used to animate or deform objects. Aside from the additional cost of calculating these displacements, they also impact the Virtual Shadow Map cache. Objects that animate need to be redrawn into the shadow map. When an object is far away from the camera, and its on-screen footprint is small, you can disable the animation to avoid these shadow map invalidations. </p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">The <b>World Position Offset Disable Distance</b> property on primitives can be set to limit the distance at which WPO is applied. </p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">The <b>Shadow Cache</b> <b>Invalidation Behavior</b> property on primitives can be used to ignore certain invalidation sources. </p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><b>Displacement Fading</b> can be used on materials. </p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-callout class="block-callout is-note"><div class="block-callout-inner"><span class="eds-icon block-callout-icon icon-info-circle text-body-secondary"></span><!----><span class="block-callout-content"><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">When WPO is used, the actual displacement is not known until the object is rendered. This means the Virtual Shadow Map cache system has to assume the object needs to be redrawn, even if the actual displacement has not changed. Replacing WPO usage with skeletal animation or modifying the instance transform avoids this pitfall.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></span></div></block-callout><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h3 id="separate-static-caching" data-previous-ids="separatestaticcaching"> Separate Static Caching </h3><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Many scenes consist of a large amount of static geometry that never moves, together with significantly smaller amounts of dynamic (or movable) geometry. If cached together, this means that the relatively cheap dynamic geometry invalidates pages that then cause the expensive static geometry to be re-rendered, just to update the dynamic portion.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">To better optimize in these cases, Virtual Shadow Maps stores what is effectively two copies of depth, one for each category of geometry. Thus, when the dynamic geometry moves, there is no need to redraw the static geometry. Instead, the cached static page can be cheaply composited on top. In cases, such as the <a data-document-id="3236880" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/valley-of-the-ancient-sample-game-for-unreal-engine">Valley of the Ancients</a> sample project, it can be a significant performance optimization as the static terrain is very expensive while the dynamic elements are relatively cheap.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">What geometry is rendered into which "layer" (static versus dynamic) is determined at runtime, and does not primarily rely on object mobility. Generally, if a mesh is a static mesh and is set to Static mobility, it will be cached as static. If a mesh has Movable mobility but is not updated, it will be moved to the static cache.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">The Virtual Shadow Map statistics are a good way to get a high level overview of how well static caching is working. In particular, the number of "invalidated" static pages should be near 0. Finding instances that are invalidating the static cache frequently and switching them to Movable is an important way to ensure the static cache remains valid.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Nanite includes an advanced visualization mode to help determine object mobility in the world, which is also useful for Virtual Shadow Maps.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="movinglights"> Moving Lights </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Stationary lights are largely cached and, as a result, can use a much higher resolution than moving lights. To account for this difference between stationary and moving lights, movable lights should have a different LOD bias than stationary lights. When a light stops moving, it does a gradual transition to the original bias. You can control the LOD bias for moving lights with the following scalability console variables:</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><ul><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><code>r.Shadow.Virtual.ResolutionLodBiasLocalMoving</code></p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><li><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><code>r.Shadow.Virtual.ResolutionLodBiasDirectionalMoving</code></p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></li><!----><!----></ul><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 id="coarsepages"> Coarse Pages </h2><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Depth buffer analysis is used as the primary method of marking pages that are needed to render. There are some systems that need to sample shadows at more arbitrary locations though, such as <a data-document-id="3224815" href="https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/volumetric-fog-in-unreal-engine">Volumetric Fog</a> and forward-rendered translucency. Most systems only need low-resolution shadow data that gets filtered and blurred through other data structures.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><block-video class="block-video"><electra-player class="d-block ratio ratio-16x9"><iframe src="https://dev.epicgames.com/community/api/cms/videos/1_t72uw7xl/embed.html"></iframe></electra-player><!----><!----></block-video><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">To accommodate shadowing in these situations, <strong>Coarse Pages</strong> are marked to ensure that at least low-resolution shadow data is available across the whole domain for sampling. Local lights simply mark the root mip page while Directional Lights can mark a series of pages at various low detail levels to form some coarse clipmaps.
Depending on the scene, coarse pages can create performance issues. This is particularly true for non-Nanite dynamic geometry since they are effectively rendering low-resolution shadows over large regions of space, which can result in draw-call bottlenecks.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">Local light coarse pages can be toggled off with <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.MarkCoarsePagesLocal</code>, if not needed.
Directional Light coarse pages can be toggled off with <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.MarkCoarsePagesDirectional</code>, or the range of clipmap levels that coarse pages are marked in can be modified with <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.FirstCoarseLevel</code> and <code>r.Shadow.Virtual.LastCoarseLevel</code>.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><h2 This can be used to find which objects are invalidating the shadow map.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></td><!----></tr><!----></tbody><!----><!----></table></div><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">By default, the Virtual Shadow Map visualizations display results for all lights at the same time. By selecting a light in the <strong>Outliner</strong>, you can view visualizations for that light.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">You can also enable visualization using the console (except in Shipping builds), which is useful for profiling and debugging a live game. If any of these are set in the editor, they override any mode selection made through the editor's user interface.</p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><div class="table-responsive"><table class="table" style="--columns-count: 2;"><!----><!----><thead><tr><th> Visualization Name </th><th> Description </th><!----></tr><!----></thead><!----><!----><!----><!----><tbody><tr><td><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler=""><code>r.Shadow.Virtual.Visualize [mode]</code></p><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----></td><td><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><!----><p internallinkhandler="">When the view mode visualization is set to Virtual Shadow Map through the Level Viewport or the console command, this command specifies which of the channels to display.
