Parts of the scene that are out-of-focus can request lower resolution shadows, as these regions will be blurred anyway. The \u003Ccode class=\"inline-code\">r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxDOFResolutionBias\u003C/code> variable defines the maximum bias that can be applied to the shadow resolution. The highest gains are expected in views with an expensive background that is heavily out of focus, like a character closeup in front of heavy moving foliage. ","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"header","content":"Shadow Projection","level":3,"settings":{"is_hidden":false,"anchor_id":12014,"anchor":{"id":12014,"name":"shadow-projection","previous_names":["shadowprojection"]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The \u003Cstrong>Shadow Projection\u003C/strong> category is the cost of sampling shadow maps using Shadow Map Ray Tracing. These passes are located under the \u003Cstrong>Lights | DirectLighting | UnbatchedLights\u003C/strong> and there will typically be one VSM projection pass per associated light. The most expensive pass is usually the main SMRT loop in \u003Cstrong>VirtualShadowMapProjection\u003C/strong>. The rest should be relatively low cost.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"image","image_id":26271183,"caption":"","alt_text":"GPU Profile Shadow Projection","image":{"id":26271183,"file_name":"shadow-projection-gpu-visualizer.png","file_size":55858,"content_type":"image/png","created_at":"2025-11-14T18:02:47.935+00:00","height":665,"width":611,"storage_key":"23d63246-7713-421d-be84-ed6a45487f6f","context":"documentation"},"storage_key":"23d63246-7713-421d-be84-ed6a45487f6f","context":"documentation","width":null,"settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Shadow projection is purely a function of the total number of shadow map samples that are taken across the screen, and performance doesn't depend on the number of pages or caching.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"When SMRT is being used, it comes down to:","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"enhanced_list","style":"unordered","items":[[{"type":"paragraph","content":"\u003Cstrong>Average lights per pixel\u003C/strong>","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"enhanced_list","style":"unordered","items":[[{"type":"paragraph","content":"The more lights touching large portions of the screen, the more expensive rendering will be. Lights covering small numbers of on-screen pixels are cheaper, although there are still some fixed costs per light.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}}],[{"type":"paragraph","content":"Care should be taken to avoid having the majority of pixels on screen taken up by several large lights.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}}]],"settings":{"is_hidden":false}}],[{"type":"paragraph","content":"\u003Cstrong>Rays per pixel\u003C/strong>","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"enhanced_list","style":"unordered","items":[[{"type":"paragraph","content":"Visible softness of shadows affects performance due to the adaptive ray count. Shadow Maps are still actively being developed. There are a number of known issues and limitations to using them currently, and they are currently targeted at high-end desktops and next-generation consoles.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"header","content":"Object Bounds","level":3,"settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The Virtual Shadow Maps page marking system uses object bounding boxes to mark which parts of the shadow map need to be rendered. If the bounding box of your mesh is set too small, you may see parts of an object having missing or incorrect shadows. However, if the bounding box is too large, it may invalidate more of the shadow map than is strictly necessary, which has a performance penalty. Therefore, the bounding box should fit tightly around the object. If your material uses World Position Offset, you need to set \u003Cb>Max World Position Offset Displacement\u003C/b> in the material or extend the mesh bounds to account for the maximum displacement. You can inspect bounding boxes with \u003Ccode class=\"inline-code\">ShowFlag.Bounds\u003C/code> or \u003Ccode class=\"inline-code\">ShowFlag.VisualizeShadowCasters\u003C/code>.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"header","content":"Multiple Lights Performance","level":3,"settings":{"is_hidden":false,"anchor_id":12018,"anchor":{"id":12018,"name":"multiple-lights-performance","previous_names":["multiplelightsperformance"]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Performance in scenes with many small local lights is still a work in progress. For the time being, the best strategy is to \u003Ca data-document-id=\"3225183\" href=\"https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/virtual-shadow-maps-in-unreal-engine?application_version=5.5\">enable one pass projection\u003C/a> and be very careful with invalidations to keep as many of the pages cached as possible. Multiple local lights will perform far better with Nanite geometry than non-Nanite geometry, so aggressively culling or disabling shadow casting on non-Nanite geometry in the distance can help a lot. In some cases it may be desirable to disable dynamic shadow casting on distant lights entirely and rely solely on screen space \u003Ca data-document-id=\"3225187\" href=\"https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/contact-shadows-in-unreal-engine\">Contact Shadows\u003C/a>.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"callout","callout_type":"note","blocks":[{"type":"paragraph","content":"In the future, better controls will be available for making algorithmic and quality tradeoffs, as well as throttling updates in these situations.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}}],"settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"header","content":"Low Poly Geometry","level":3,"settings":{"is_hidden":false,"anchor_id":12019,"anchor":{"id":12019,"name":"low-poly-geometry","previous_names":["lowpolygeometry"]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Low poly geometry with high curvature and smooth normals can exhibit artifacts. This is known as the \"shadow terminator problem.\" It also occurs in ray tracing and other highly accurate visibility queries. The issue stems from the mismatch between the real low poly geometry and the \"smooth\" shading normals: in the area near the terminator some of these faces are geometrically in shadow, but the non-geometric shading normals are slightly facing the light. It is common to work around this artifact with a normal-based bias to the shadow lookup. This particular artifact can be more noticeable with Virtual Shadow Maps because by default they are set up to deliver highly detailed shadows from Nanite geometry.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The best way to address this is to increase the polygon count in these objects/regions. Limiting the divergence between the geometric and shading normals reduces or eliminates these artifacts without negatively impacting shadow quality elsewhere. With Nanite adding more polygons is straightforward and generally inexpensive. If the offending objects cannot use Nanite, adding a higher detail level of detail (LOD) often works well too, as these artifacts are mostly visible when objects are near the camera.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If it is not possible to add more geometry, the Virtual Shadow Map normal bias can be increased using \u003Ccode>r.Shadow.Virtual.NormalBias\u003C/code> (default 0.5). Note that this should only be considered when content adjustments are not possible as it will negatively impact the quality of shadows throughout the scene, but particularly in areas of fine detail.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"In the examples below, artifacts are visible on a low polygon sphere near the camera with high detail geometry in the background. Adding polygons to the sphere improves the artifacts without negatively affecting the detailed landscape in the Virtual Shadow Maps, all of the shadow data in the scene for all lights is stored in a single large texture pool. The default pool size is affected by the \u003Cstrong>Shadow\u003C/strong> Scalability setting, but it may need to be adjusted in scenes with many lights using high resolution shadows.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Alternatively it may need to be adjusted on lower-end hardware to save video memory.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"The page pool size can be adjusted using \u003Ccode>r.Shadow.Virtual.MaxPhysicalPages\u003C/code>. Enabling Virtual Shadow Map stats with \u003Ccode>r.ShaderPrintEnable 1\u003C/code> and \u003Ccode>r.Shadow.Virtual.ShowStats 2\u003C/code>, in succession, will display statistics about the current page pool use.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"image","image_id":26271184,"caption":"Example of current page pool use from Virtual Shadow Map on-screen stats.","alt_text":"VSM physical pages stat","image":{"id":26271184,"file_name":"vsm-physical-page-pool.png","file_size":46178,"content_type":"image/png","created_at":"2025-11-14T18:02:48.053+00:00","height":106,"width":333,"storage_key":"3fd5d732-8d0f-4520-9a62-a3b0083d03ec","context":"documentation"},"storage_key":"3fd5d732-8d0f-4520-9a62-a3b0083d03ec","context":"documentation","width":null,"settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If the number of \u003Cstrong>Pages\u003C/strong> exceeds \u003Cstrong>Max Pages\u003C/strong> corruption will occur, which sometimes manifests visually as a checkerboard pattern, or corrupt or missing shadows. If the shadow page pool overflows, a warning is displayed on screen and in the log.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"image","image_id":26271185,"caption":"Example of corrupted virtual shadow maps from an exceeded number of pages in the page pool.","alt_text":"max pages exceeded artifact","image":{"id":26271185,"file_name":"vsm-max-pages-exceeded-artifact.png","file_size":736758,"content_type":"image/png","created_at":"2025-11-14T18:02:48.113+00:00","height":692,"width":996,"storage_key":"0fa07dd2-ccf2-4eec-92dd-64e27aba7b90","context":"documentation"},"storage_key":"0fa07dd2-ccf2-4eec-92dd-64e27aba7b90","context":"documentation","width":null,"settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"If this occurs, increase the size of the page pool or decrease the shadow resolution or number of virtual shadow map casting lights.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"header","content":"Materials","level":3,"settings":{"is_hidden":false,"anchor_id":12024,"anchor":{"id":12024,"name":"materials","previous_names":["materials"]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Only simple subsurface materials are supported. Subsurface Profile and transmission are not yet implemented. If a material is using them, that material will be shadowed as though it is opaque.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"header","content":"Shadow Resolution","level":3,"settings":{"is_hidden":false,"anchor_id":12025,"anchor":{"id":12025,"name":"shadow-resolution","previous_names":["shadowresolution"]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Virtual Shadow Maps provide significantly increased resolution compared to conventional shadow maps, but shallow light angles (or projective aliasing) and very large local lights can exhaust the available virtual resolution. This may present itself as box-like shadows and bias issues depending on the geometry's surface.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"Directional Light clipmaps are much less susceptible to running out of resolution, but very narrow camera fields-of-view can eventually exhaust those as well.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"There is no simple solution to solving projective aliasing with shadow maps. Even with virtual shadow maps, some care must be taken to avoid the worst cases and balance resolution with performance.","settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"header","content":"Unsupported Geometry","level":3,"settings":{"is_hidden":false}},{"type":"paragraph","content":"While the vast majority of geometry types are supported, there are a few types that are not. By default, these unsupported geometry types will simply not cast shadows.
